pages.text: "I don't need to wash! I'm not dirty!" Soso the quiet hedgehog backed away from the big wooden tub. Steam rose from it. Between Soso's spines, stream mud had dried hard.
"When they're wet, my spines droop. I don't want anyone to see." On the slope, everyone was playing at rolling. "I want to roll like a ball too..."
At the top, Soso tried to curl up. But dried mud stuck the spines together. No rolling all the way—just roll, bump. Then a stop.
Mei the timid baby goat rolled smoothly past. Soso sat on the slope, only half curled. The stuck-together spines stung.
The sun shone hard. The mud dried even harder. Soso tried to straighten their back. "Ouch!" The spines tugged. Soso pouted.
Grandma Bear dissolved soap in the big wooden tub behind the lodge and stirred. White bubbles billowed up. She sang, "Bubbles on my spines—pop, pop!"
Soso dipped their toes in gently. The water was warm. A bubble appeared at each spine tip. Pop, pop, pop! "Oh? I can't see my spines!"
The hard mud loosened and sank into the water. In the tub, Soso curled round, then stretched out. "I'm round! I can curl round!"
As water poured over Soso, they called loudly, "One, toes in first! Two, bubbles on every spine! Three, pour water and rinse!" Water dripped from the spines.
Soso rolled across the grassy slope, farthest of all. Grandma wrapped Soso in a dry towel. After washing, dry spines stand up again. "Grandma, tomorrow too—bubbles on my spines, pop, pop!"
